subject: Re: Model fit & tool-calling evals - next steps and schema QA
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@finapp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 03 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Model fit & tool-calling evals - post-call recap and next steps

Thanks for taking the time this morning, Olivia - really useful conversation. Quick recap + proposed next steps from our side: 

1) Goals we heard
- FinApp wants reliable, low-latency structured responses for transaction categorization and policy tagging (JSON outputs).
- Must meet a JSON-schema validation rate >= 98% across representative production prompts.
- Need graceful retries and fallback behavior when downstream function calls fail (e.g., payment API timeout).

2) Recommended model candidates (based on preliminary evals)
- redwood/gpt-optim-7b (best balance of latency/cost for real-time needs)
- redwood/gpt-optim-13b-q4 (higher quality for edge cases; consider for batch/canary)
- For high-throughput batch jobs we can recommend a quantized 13B profile we tested.

3) Tool / function-calling notes
- We validated function-calling stubs with our harness - key concerns are (a) JSON schema compliance, (b) deterministic field ordering for downstream parsers, (c) retry idempotency when side-effectful functions are involved.
- We suggest a primary strategy: try the best-fit model with strict schema constraints; if schema validation fails after 1 retry, fall back to the 13B variant and mark the event for manual review.

4) Deliverables we'll provide this week
- prompt_set_v3.json (attached) - 120 representative prompts mapping to expected schema examples
- baseline benchmark link with latency/p99 and schema pass rates (link below)
- a short eval harness CSV export (finapp_eval_results.csv) with example outputs and failure cases

5) Next steps / ask
- Can you share a sanitized sample of 100 recent prompts (~no PII) and confirm whether your downstream calls are idempotent?
- We propose a technical deep-dive next Tue/Wed with your engineering + our Marissa (eval lead) to align on acceptance criteria and the sandbox runbook.

Links: https://docs.redwood.ai/benchmarks/model-fit-2026

Attachments: prompt_set_v3.json, finapp_eval_results.csv, schema_examples.json

Thanks - I'll coordinate calendar invites once you confirm the time slots.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0142

From: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@finapp.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: FinApp Platform Team <platform@finapp.com>
Date: Thu, 03 Dec 2026 12:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Model fit & tool-calling evals - post-call recap and next steps

Thanks Neha - appreciate the clear recap. A few follow-ups from our side: 

- JSON schema compliance: our downstream processors are strict. When the model returns invalid JSON we currently drop the record. We can change to a retry+flag flow, but need to understand the expected failure modes and how many retries you recommend.
- Retries and idempotency: our payment tagging call is idempotent for 'tag' operations but there are a couple of side-effectful endpoints; we will share which ones are side-effectful before the deep dive.
- Sample prompts: we can produce a 100-prompt export (sanitized) by EOD Monday.

One quick ask: can you give an example of the structured-output acceptance criteria you mentioned (e.g., exact fields, types, and validation rules)? Also curious what the p99 latency numbers look like for the 7B option under a typical 50 qps workload.

Thanks - Olivia
Olivia Chen
Head of Platform
FinApp
olivia.chen@finapp.com | (617) 555-0199

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@finapp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 03 Dec 2026 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Model fit & tool-calling evals - post-call recap and next steps

Great - thanks Olivia. Answers inline and a couple more details: 

- Acceptance criteria (example):
  - Required output fields: {"transaction_id": string, "category": string, "confidence": number (0-1), "policy_flags": [string]}
  - Type validation: strict JSON schema enforced by our eval harness. Pass = schema validation + confidence >= 0.65 for automated tagging.
  - JSON pass-rate target for pilot: >= 98% across the 100-sample set; gateway fallbacks allowed for the remainder.

- Retries: we recommend 1 immediate retry on schema parse failure (same model, new generation) and 1 fallback generation on the 13B variant if the retry also fails. For side-effectful downstream calls, use a dry-run/predict-only mode from the model to validate payloads before executing the external API.

- Latency (p99) for redwood/gpt-optim-7b at 50 qps (our internal benchmark): ~420ms p99 on our dedicated cluster (NVidia H100 equivalent), with batching tuned for 50 qps. Expect slightly higher on smaller GPUs or noisy multi-tenant hosts. Link to detailed benchmark: https://docs.redwood.ai/benchmarks/model-fit-2026#7b

- Artifacts: prompt_set_v3.json (attached) includes expected JSON examples and negative cases. We also attached schema_examples.json with the exact JSON Schema draft-07 we run.

Marissa will take point on the eval harness run - Marissa, can you add the test matrix (schema pass, retry behavior, fallback success) and propose windows for the sandbox run?

Olivia - once you send the sanitized prompts and the list of side-effectful endpoints we'll scope the sandbox and SLOs for the pilot.

Best,
Neha

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@finapp.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 04 Dec 2026 11:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Model fit & tool-calling evals - post-call recap and next steps

Thanks Neha / Olivia - I'll run the structured-output evals once we have the sanitized 100 prompts and the list of side-effectful endpoints. Quick plan: 

- Eval matrix (pilot):
  - JSON schema pass-rate (target >= 98%)
  - Retry success rate: fraction of schema failures that pass after 1 retry (target >= 60%)
  - Fallback success: fraction of remaining failures resolved by the 13B fallback (target >= 50%)
  - Latency: p50/p95/p99 for primary model under the sandbox config

- Test harness: I'll run 3 replica runs (different seeds) to surface non-deterministic failures and produce finapp_eval_results.csv with per-prompt outputs + failure tags.

- Proposed windows for the sandbox run next week (PST): Tue 12/07 10-11am or Wed 12/08 2-3pm. Please confirm a preferred slot and I'll send a calendar invite.

HubSpot: linked to DEAL-4382 (https://redwood.hubspot.com/deal/DEAL-4382) - I'll add the eval artifacts there once the run completes.

Marissa Cole
Lead, Model Evaluation & Onboarding
Redwood Inference
